strengths: Novel Stochastic Multimodal Fusion framework that effectively captures redundant, unique, and synergistic information across modalities, with theoretical justification (Lemma 1) and empirical validation through synthetic data experiments

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation: 41 diverse urban prediction tasks across 56 cities worldwide with proper statistical controls, comprehensive ablation studies, and cross-regional generalization experiments
Robust to realistic incomplete modality scenarios (Table 6), maintaining strong performance even with 25% data availability, critical for real-world deployment
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, dataset construction protocols, hyperparameter specifications, code/model release planned, enabling future research
Clear practical contribution as first urban-specific multimodal location encoder addressing genuine gaps in geospatial ML for urban prediction tasks
Consistent performance improvements across diverse task domains (regression and classification) and geographic regions, demonstrating broad applicability
Strong theoretical grounding in information decomposition with partial information decomposition (PID) framework formalizing modality-specific, shared, and synergistic components
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: individual components (Vision Transformers, contrastive learning, reconstruction losses) are established techniques; random modality masking, while effective, is relatively straightforward
Task-specific improvements often modest (2-4% gains in R² over GAIR baselines on many tasks); missing analysis of when multimodal fusion is necessary vs. when single modalities suffice

Geographic bias in evaluation: heavy focus on developed nations (North America, Europe, wealthy Asia); limited evaluation in Global South, developing countries, or less-urbanized regions; generalization claims would benefit from more diverse evaluation

Incomplete theoretical justification: Assumption 1 (proxy modality existence) is strong and not universally validated; why random masking is optimal for information decomposition not thoroughly explained; temperature parameter τ appears empirically chosen without principled justification

Limited ablation studies on critical design choices: loss weight balance between contrastive and reconstruction objectives not systematically explored; masking probability not ablated; alternative Transformer fusion architectures not compared
Computational cost analysis limited to forward pass timing; training memory requirements unclear; scalability with very large modality vocabularies not addressed

No analysis of failure cases or task characteristics predicting when multimodal fusion helps most; some specialized baselines (e.g., PDFM for ZIP codes) outperform UrbanFusion on specific tasks without investigation

Statistical rigor gaps: linear probing results often lack confidence intervals despite MLP results including error bars; no formal statistical significance testing despite potential overlapping confidence intervals
Incomplete modality handling validated primarily through synthetic data; real-world missing data patterns (e.g., entire cities lacking street view) not thoroughly evaluated
